title: Shared-module findings reduction and prioritized implementation backlog

completedFoundations.summary: Shared HTTP request helpers were created.
Shared search/risk request helpers were created.
Shared JSON file helpers were created.
Shared JSON gate harness tooling was created.
Shared-module boundary guardrails and waivers now fail on new architecture drift.
Manifest-driven migration codemod support now exists for repeated import rewrites.

priorityBatches.whyNow: The new boundary guard is already tracking runtime src/** -> tools/shared/** debt. Eliminating the remaining waived edges gives the biggest immediate architecture payoff and lets the guard become stricter.

items.title: Migrate remaining runtime consumers off tools/shared/dict-utils.js
items.bestFix: Use the new migration codemod where possible, then shrink src/shared/dict-utils.js into a real canonical owner instead of a compatibility bridge.

items.title: Eliminate the last runtime import of tools/shared/search-request.js
items.bestFix: Move the caller fully to src/shared/search-request.js and delete the temporary wrapper once no consumers remain.

items.title: Hoist or replace tools/shared/index-state-utils.js for runtime sqlite usage
items.bestFix: Move the reusable state logic into a canonical src/shared or storage-local helper so runtime storage code no longer depends on tools/shared.

priorityBatches.whyNow: The root src/shared bucket still mixes generic helpers, domain owners, and compatibility bridges. This is the biggest source of future drift after the explicit tools/shared runtime debt.

items.title: Split env/runtime/policy helpers out of src/shared root
items.bestFix: Create clearer family ownership for environment/runtime policy instead of leaving them in the generic root bucket.

items.title: Relocate root-only domain shims and re-exports
items.bestFix: Remove cross-layer re-exports and move specialized helpers to their owning subsystem or shared family.

items.title: Split large root-level domain helpers into narrower families
items.bestFix: Move language, embeddings, indexing-pointer, and timeout-policy owners into domain-specific shared families so dependencies and tests become easier to reason about.

priorityBatches.whyNow: Artifact/cache/io helpers are heavily imported and currently carry too many responsibilities. Splitting them improves both reviewability and the safety of future storage/indexing changes.

items.title: Break up artifact-io manifest and loader cores
items.bestFix: Separate manifest description, cache lookup, filesystem helpers, and loader orchestration so each piece has a narrower API.

items.title: Split generic bundle/file/persistence helpers by responsibility
items.bestFix: Untangle write orchestration, path helpers, and atomic persistence contracts into smaller focused modules.

items.title: Move schema-oriented helpers out of generic storage buckets
items.bestFix: Treat schema and docmeta helpers as contract-domain modules rather than generic artifact IO utilities.

priorityBatches.whyNow: These modules sit on critical execution paths. Their current size and mixed responsibilities increase the risk of regressions in queueing, process supervision, and progress semantics.

items.title: Split correctness-critical subprocess and lock modules
items.bestFix: Separate state tracking, process execution, and lock-file semantics into smaller units with tighter targeted tests.

items.title: Deflate generic progress and scheduler-core controllers
items.bestFix: Split event formatting from policy/control logic so concurrency tuning and progress presentation do not evolve inside the same module.

priorityBatches.whyNow: This family is important, but the work is less correctness-sensitive than the runtime and storage batches above.

items.title: Split display/render and command registry surfaces
items.bestFix: Separate presentation, command metadata, and capability-manifest projection so UI and dispatch consumers do not depend on one giant module seam.

items.title: Relocate dispatch environment helpers away from tools/shared coupling
items.bestFix: Finish the move away from tools/shared and collapse thin wrappers that do not provide independent value.

priorityBatches.whyNow: The scan artifacts identified many duplicate clusters, but not all of them deserve immediate action. This batch should target the highest-frequency seams first.

items.title: Prioritize repeated repo/workspace/path/env handling seams
items.bestFix: Batch the repo/workspace identity and path/env normalization migrations first because they influence many other consumer surfaces.

items.title: Target repeated search/report/progress/logging clusters next
items.bestFix: Use the duplicate-cluster seed list from the ledger to drive the next round of narrow shared-module creation or adoption, rather than scanning ad hoc.

deferOrDrop.title: Do not generalize every duplicate filename stem into a shared module
deferOrDrop.reason: Many stem collisions in the ledger are domain-local and would create weak abstractions if hoisted prematurely.

deferOrDrop.title: Do not expand the codemod beyond exact-specifier migrations until a stable seam is proven
deferOrDrop.reason: Broad AST rewrites would create more review risk than value at this stage.

deferOrDrop.title: Do not tighten the tools/shared boundary beyond the current waiver-backed rule until the remaining debt is removed
deferOrDrop.reason: The current guard is intentionally narrow to avoid noisy false positives while migration work is still active.
